newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mixed on uncertainties.

text.p: Shanghai Soybean futures ended mixed on Thursday investor uncertainties over the short-term market trend, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 3,305 yuan ($398) per tonne, losing 5 yuan. It opened at 3,310 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,316 and a low of 3,304.
July rose one yuan to 3,256, September fell eight to 3,302, the January 1998 contract rose 68 to 3,240.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around the opening level for most of the session, traders said.
"Retail investors dominated today's trading and opinions are mixed about the short-term market trend," one trader said.
"In addition, investors seem to be satisfied with soybean movements around 3,300 yuan in the short term," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
